title: VDBE index-record rowid extraction and prefix comparison

scope.rationale: sqlite3VdbeIdxRowid and sqlite3VdbeIdxKeyCompare acquire untrusted encoded index records, validate/decode the final integer rowid or compare the prefix against an unpacked key, and release temporary payload ownership on every post-read path.
excluded_responsibilities: Raw pager/B-tree payload acquisition outside the materialized native cursor

external_source_responsibilities: Valid Btree cursor and complete payload acquisition into temporary Mem
dependencies.caller_closure: The complete bodies are assigned. Production materialized B-tree cursors own full payload acquisition, and index seek plus IdxRowid opcode paths invoke these validators.

inputs: Database connection, valid Btree index cursor, and rowid output
outputs: OK with decoded rowid, cursor/payload error, or CORRUPT for malformed header/final serial value
contracts.ownership: Cursor is borrowed; temporary full-record Mem allocation is released on success and corruption.
contracts.state_and_results: Header size must be 3 through record length. Final header serial type must be integer 1 through 9 excluding 7, and its payload must fit at the record tail.
contracts.locks_callbacks_io: Caller owns Btree cursor locks. One full payload read may perform pager I/O.
contracts.failure_and_continuation: Payload errors propagate. Malformed records return CORRUPT after cleanup without publishing rowid.

representation_differences: The native B-tree cursor materializes and owns complete record payloads when opened, so these owners borrow exact payload slices instead of allocating a temporary Mem per call.
indexRowid reads the final header byte directly like source; indexKeyCompare streams exactly the requested prefix against typed unpacked fields.

oracle.protocol: Promotion requires a pinned-C/Zig matrix over valid integer serial types 1-6/8/9, malformed header sizes, forbidden serial types, truncated rowid payloads, payload errors, and cleanup state.
internal_observations: temporary payload ownership and unchanged output on failure
oracle.normalization: Cursor transport may be normalized to exact payload bytes only after payload error and cleanup behavior is separately retained.

assurance.oom: No per-call allocation after cursor materialization; cursor-opening allocation has bounded B-tree coverage.
assurance.io_crash_concurrency: Materialized cursor payload transport is integrated, but exact pinned-C cursor error/cleanup trace remains pending.
assurance.malformed_input: Direct tests cover valid serial 1/8/9 plus short header, forbidden serial, truncated integer, and zero payload; broad record tests cover all serial classes.
assurance.continuation: Rowid publishes only after validation; comparison errors do not mutate the cursor or key.
assurance.performance: One direct final-header/record-tail decode for rowid and one streaming prefix pass for key comparison.

integration.production_owner: src/core/internal/record_compare.zig through materialized src/core/btree.zig Cursor payload ownership
integration.native_call_path: Production B-tree seek and VDBE IdxRowid call the translated slice owners; exact source cursor transport equivalence remains unpromoted.
integration.bounded_owner_retired: No separate simplified rowid/prefix decoder remains.

independent_review.notes: Requires source translation, payload/cursor trace, integration assurance, and independent review.

known_blockers: Run the exact pinned-C malformed/integer-serial and cursor-error trace before internal-trace promotion.
External pager/cursor I/O assurance remains broader than this materialized payload boundary.
